summary: Fine-tuning makes the most sense after prompt engineering and RAG have been exhausted — the canonical 2026 sequence is Prompt → RAG → Fine-tune → Distill, moving right only when the cheaper option provably hits a wall. Most production systems layer all three, with fine-tuning reserved for cases where behavior remains inconsistent at scale, domain-specific style or tone must be deeply embedded, or latency constraints make large prompt contexts impractical. The bar for needing fine-tuning keeps rising as base models like Qwen3, Llama 4, and Gemma 3 handle tasks out of the box that required fine-tuning 18 months ago.
when_to_fine_tune: Choose fine-tuning when prompt engineering and RAG both fail to produce consistent, reliable behavior at production scale — not as a first resort.
Fine-tune when you need the model to internalize a specific tone, style, or domain vocabulary so deeply that repeated prompting or retrieval cannot replicate it efficiently.
Fine-tune when latency or cost constraints make large context windows (stuffed with RAG results or few-shot examples) untenable in production.
Fine-tune for RLHF/alignment use cases, instruction-following customization, or when distilling a large model's capabilities into a smaller, faster, cheaper deployment target.
